problem: The bounded operations evaluator passed the workbook date-system flag, but every date/time calendar helper used a hard-coded 1900 epoch. Native 1904 DATE results were 1462 days too large in XLS/XLSX/XLSB. Native SUM(Table1[Quantity]) also manufactured zero when no table was registered, because the unresolved table name became a scalar error discarded by aggregation.
changes: Thread the workbook date-system flag through date constructors, text-date coercion, component/week/difference operations, offsets, workday/networkday endpoints and holiday ranges, and raw-engine current-date/time serialization. Keep pure time fractions independent of the date epoch.

Refuse explicit structured-reference syntax without a registered table with a typed UnsupportedContent error. Bare identifiers still fall through to defined-name resolution; registered tables and names remain evaluable. The operations layer reports Calc(Unsupported) instead of zero for the native table formula.

Add five native integration tests over 15 Excel specimens, including both file-backed Auto and Eager routes for core reads/calculations. Add two date-system unit regressions and one registered/unregistered-table/name unit regression.

Correct an older calculation test that still expected five absent XLS string caches. A raw BIFF audit found twelve FORMULA records and seven corresponding STRING payloads; the current reader exposes all twelve caches. The revised test asserts all seven exact strings.

Index the concrete native tests and review the three complete-Excel-evaluation rows as explicit compatibility boundaries. A bounded evaluator exists and must be correct within its tested profile; that does not imply complete Excel behavior.

verification_scope.native_1904_dates: B5 DATE(2024,2,29) computes 43889, B6 DATE+TIME computes 44848.5515625, and B8 TIME computes 0.2708333333333333. Cached and computed origins are distinct, all three formulas match their native caches, and evaluation leaves complete source archives exact in all three formats and both ingress modes.
verification_scope.date_function_consistency: Focused tests use both date systems and verify the 1462-day serial difference while calendar results remain the same: DATE, DATEVALUE, EDATE, EOMONTH, WORKDAY/WORKDAY.INTL, YEAR/MONTH/DAY, weekday/week-number functions, DAYS/DATEDIF/DAYS360/YEARFRAC, TIME/HOUR and holiday-range NETWORKDAYS variants. Existing 1900 compatibility behavior is not broadened into an early-1900 edge-case guarantee.
verification_scope.native_caches_and_shared_formulas: Native products, SUM and AVERAGE match caches. A library scalar derivative keeps the D2 cache at 3.75 while explicit computation returns 5 and D6 returns 51; save/reopen retains that distinction. Shared ROW()*2 at D4/D53/D103 returns 8/106/206. Metadata error caches retain #VALUE! and #DIV/0!, and all nine metadata formulas agree with caches. Read-only evaluation never publishes computed caches.
verification_scope.unsupported_results: External B2/B3 and dependent B4 preserve caches 49.75/14/63.75 but return precise Calc(Unsupported) errors and report entries with no computed value. Native concatenation remains unsupported. Native XLSX SUM(Table1[Quantity]) retains cache 14 and now refuses without a registered table. Direct-engine tests also cover explicit column/#All/empty-table syntax, successful table registration after refusal, and bare defined-name fallback.
verification_scope.limits_and_volatile_derivatives: A one-cell quota returns Calc(Limit Cells observed=2 maximum=1) without changing bytes or subsequent valid evaluation. A library-authored uncached XLSX NOW formula returns Calc(Volatile). An existing XLSB formula changed to NOW retains cache 30 and returns it even for explicit recalculation; each derivative reports one volatile formula. The XLS cell writer deliberately admits its narrower 14-function set and refuses NOW with exact InvalidValue/property/message. The XLSB derivative reuses A7 because its native calculation chain forbids adding a new formula cell; no guard was bypassed.
verification_scope.legacy_validation_correction: The existing ComplexFunctionTestCaseData.xls test now asserts all twelve cached matches and exact STRING values 3+4i, 3+4j, i, 1, 2+3i, -2-3i and -0.5-3.2i. This corrects a stale expectation against the current reader; no input or reader behavior was changed for that result.
verification_scope.scope_boundaries: xls-193, xlsx-270 and xlsb-331 remain uncovered universal-compatibility rows with explicit supported/unsupported scopes and linked evidence. Concrete checks are credited only to their formula/cache/link rows. Unknown syntax, arbitrary dependency/spill engines, external functions/providers, automatic cache synchronization and native-application equivalence remain outside the claim.
verification_scope.limits: No fresh Excel reopen/recalculation, macro/control execution, external refresh, clock/random use by the operations evaluator, complete formula grammar, table discovery in the operations grid, arbitrary future compatibility or full early-1900 calendar emulation is claimed.
